rules.title: Annotation argument literal kinds
rules.statement: An annotation argument literal is one of: integer, float, bool, string, enum-variant (Name::Variant), or array of literals. Arrays are parsed recursively element-by-element.

rules.title: Float annotation literal: strip underscores and f32/f64 suffix
rules.statement: A float annotation literal has all '_' separators removed and an optional trailing 'f32'/'f64' suffix stripped before parsing to a double.

rules.title: String annotation literal escape decoding
rules.statement: A quoted string annotation literal has surrounding quotes stripped and escapes \n \t \r \\ \" \0 decoded; an unrecognised escape is preserved verbatim (backslash + char). A raw string r"..." strips the r" prefix and trailing quote with no escape processing.

rules.title: Bare annotation #[A] takes no arguments
rules.statement: An annotation written #[A] (no ARGS, no VALUE) produces an instance with an empty argument list.

rules.title: #[A = lit] binds first field
rules.statement: An annotation #[A = lit] maps the single value to the annotation datatype's first declared field; if the datatype has no fields it is an error ('annotation takes no arguments').

rules.title: Positional annotation args bind by declaration order
rules.statement: Positional arguments in #[A(arg, ...)] bind to the annotation datatype's fields in declaration order; supplying more positional args than fields is an error ('takes at most N positional args').

rules.title: Named annotation args bind by field name
rules.statement: A named argument key=value in #[A(...)] binds to the field whose name equals the key; an unknown field name is an error ('has no field') but does not abort parsing of remaining args.

rules.title: User annotation NAME must be an #[annotation]-marked datatype
rules.statement: An annotation whose name is not a compiler-internal key is treated as a user annotation only if NAME resolves to a registered datatype carrying the IS_ANNOTATION_TYPE marker; otherwise it is silently ignored.

rules.title: Annotations and doc-comments accumulate until next item
rules.statement: Annotation nodes accumulate in a pending buffer and are consumed by the next non-annotation item; doc-comment lines/blocks (///, /**, //!, /*!) similarly accumulate. Both buffers are cleared after each item.

rules.title: #[type_code=N] on struct/datatype sets type code
rules.statement: #[type_code=N] on a struct or datatype sets the type's TYPE_CODE to N and registers N under the fully-qualified name (pkg::Name) in the explicit-type-code table so type_code_of::<T>() resolves cross-package.

rules.title: #[tag_dispatch(system)] on trait sets dispatch system name
rules.statement: #[tag_dispatch(system_name)] on a trait records system_name as the trait's TAG_DISPATCH_SYSTEM, identifying the tagged-dispatch system the trait participates in.

rules.title: #[type_code=N] on trait marks it a genos
rules.statement: #[type_code=N] on a trait sets the trait's TYPE_CODE: the code names the logical datatype family, and each `impl Trait for Eidos` propagates it to the target struct during lowering.

rules.title: #[type_code] forbidden on parametric (template) genos
rules.statement: #[type_code=N] on a parametric genos (trait with non-empty type params) is an error; the code must be attached to a concrete specialization, else every specialization would collide in the same tag-system slot.

rules.title: Structural struct flags are set-only (monotonic)
rules.statement: Structural attributes #[zone_mut], #[zoned2], #[rel_ptr], #[self_describing], #[borrow_carrying] each set the corresponding boolean struct flag when present; a present flag can only set, never clear, the base value.

rules.title: #[zoned] struct lowered as a datatype (zoned struct)
rules.statement: A struct carrying #[zoned] (promotes_to_datatype) is lowered with IS_ZONED set, treated as a zoned struct/datatype rather than a plain struct.

rules.title: datatype/eidos is always zoned
rules.statement: A `datatype` (eidos) definition is always lowered with IS_ZONED set, including its specializations, unconditionally (unlike a plain struct which requires #[zoned]).

rules.title: Auto type-code from name hash for concrete zoned types
rules.statement: A concrete (non-generic) zoned struct/datatype with TYPE_CODE==0 receives an auto-assigned code from the 56-bit hash of its canonical name pkg::Name; codes < 128 are bumped by +128 to stay outside the reserved inline-AnyVal range 1..127. Generic templates are hashed at instantiation time.

rules.title: instantiate decl requires a generic target with type args
rules.statement: `instantiate T;` requires T to be a struct/datatype/enum with non-empty type args; `instantiate Foo;` on a non-generic type is an error ('only applies to generic templates'), and a non-struct/datatype/enum target is an error.

rules.title: Explicit struct/datatype instantiation requires concrete type args
rules.statement: A bodyless `struct Foo<args>;` / `datatype Foo<args>;` (NAME absent, TYPE present) is an explicit instantiation: type args must be concrete (no unbound type vars), else it is an error directing to write the body; a bare `struct Foo;` referencing an undefined name is also an error.

rules.title: genos specialization decl propagates type_code to like-named eidos
rules.statement: A bodyless `genos Name<args>;` (trait-name TYPE, no NAME) records an instantiation annotation; its #[type_code=N] is registered under the canonical and mangled (concrete-struct) names of the like-named eidos/struct, mirrored under both the current and the template's package.

rules.title: union lowered through struct path
rules.statement: A `union` definition is lowered through the same path as a struct (same field shape); layout/unsafe-gating is a separate concern.

rules.title: extern block children flattened into item stream
rules.statement: An extern block's child items (extern fn declarations) are spliced in order into the flat module-item worklist; the block itself produces no item.

rules.title: Outer doc-comments (/// and /**) attach to next item
rules.statement: `///` line doc-comments (with leading '/// ' stripped, joined by newline) and `/** ... */` outer block doc-comments accumulate into the pending doc buffer and become the DOC of the next item.

rules.title: cfg attributes gate item lowering
rules.statement: An item whose pending cfg attributes evaluate false (cfg_attrs_drop_item) is dropped before lowering; its pending annotations and doc are consumed and discarded.

rules.title: #[test] / #[ignore] / #[should_panic] flag functions
rules.statement: On a function, #[test] marks it a test, #[ignore] marks it ignored, and #[should_panic] marks expect-panic; #[should_panic(expected="msg")] records the expected panic substring (string literal, quotes stripped). These flags are reset per-function before reading.

rules.title: static gets global storage with symbol, mut/extern flags
rules.statement: A `static` item is lowered with IS_STATIC set, real global storage keyed by a module-qualified symbol (fallback pkg$name); `static mut` sets IS_MUT; a static lacking VALUE is extern (IS_EXTERN, no initializer emitted).

rules.title: const carries an inlined value expression
rules.statement: A `const` item stores its initializer as a VALUE expression that downstream codegen inlines at each use site (contrasted with statics, which have one global per item).

rules.title: Module inner doc (//! and /*! */) commits once per module
rules.statement: `//!` line and `/*! ... */` block inner doc-comments accumulate (leading marker stripped, blocks joined by newline) into a per-module buffer over the whole item-lowering pass; after all items are processed, if non-empty, the buffer is committed as a single ModuleInnerDoc record (keyed by the module's file path) on the program and reset.
